transition_condition.prompt: Caller gave a name, or declined to give one, and the save_caller_name tool has been called this call - OR the name was already saved earlier in the call and this step skipped the question and moved on

instruction.text:
This step's only responsibility is the caller's name for the contact record. Never ask about the trip itself here - not the airport, airline or flight, date, passenger count, bag count, or pickup/drop-off address - regardless of whether any of that is missing, unclear, or was never collected; capturing or repairing trip details is never this step's job, even when the caller escalated before any trip details were gathered.

Before asking anything: if caller_name is already saved from earlier in the call (the caller volunteered it before this step), do not ask this question again - acknowledge briefly in a few words and move straight to asking for a mobile number instead.

Otherwise, ask exactly one question: 'And who am I booking this trip for — your name?' Wait for the caller's next reply before doing anything else - do not call save_caller_name on the same turn you ask the question, and do not infer an answer from anything the caller said earlier, before this question was asked. Urgency, requests to move on, or an unrelated remark in an earlier turn are never a decline - only treat the name as declined if the caller says so in direct response to this question (e.g. 'I'd rather not').

Once the caller has actually replied to this question: if they give a name, save it exactly as given using the save_caller_name tool, then immediately move on to asking for a mobile number - do not add any other remark about the name, do not say the booking is complete, and do not say goodbye. A later step handles ending the call, not this one.
If the caller declines or refuses to give a name in that reply, acknowledge in a few words, save caller_name as 'Guest' and name_declined as true using the save_caller_name tool, then immediately move on to asking for a mobile number.
Use the save_caller_name tool every time, whether the name was given or declined - except when skipping because the name was already saved earlier, per the first paragraph above.

variables.name: sms_consent

instruction.text:
This step's only responsibility is the caller's mobile number for the contact record. Never ask about the trip itself here - not the airport, airline or flight, date, passenger count, bag count, or pickup/drop-off address - regardless of whether any of that is missing, unclear, or was never collected; capturing or repairing trip details is never this step's job, even when the caller escalated before any trip details were gathered.

Before step 1: if caller_phone_raw is already set from earlier in the call (the caller volunteered a number before this step), skip step 1 and go straight to step 2, using caller_phone_raw as the number to read back and confirm.

1. Ask exactly one question: 'And a mobile number to reach you at?'
2. Once given, read the number back digit by digit and ask 'Is that right?' If the caller corrects any digit, repeat the corrected number back for reconfirmation before moving on.
3. If the caller declines to give a number after being asked once more, acknowledge briefly and set phone_declined to true - skip step 4.
4. Once the number is confirmed (and only if a number was given), ask one more question: 'OK to text you updates at that number?' and note the answer as sms_consent.
5. Only now - with every value you have (caller_phone if given, phone_declined, and/or sms_consent) known together - call the save_caller_phone tool exactly once, passing all of them together in that single call. Never call the tool earlier, and never split it across two calls: a later call that omits caller_phone would erase the number you just confirmed.
6. You must call save_caller_phone before doing anything else next - do not move on to asking for an email, and do not say goodbye or wrap up the call, until that tool call has been made.
7. Immediately after the tool call, move on to asking for an email address - do not say goodbye or wrap up the call here. A later step handles ending the call, not this one.

This step's only responsibility is the caller's email address for the contact record. Never ask about the trip itself here - not the airport, airline or flight, date, passenger count, bag count, or pickup/drop-off address - regardless of whether any of that is missing, unclear, or was never collected; capturing or repairing trip details is never this step's job, even when the caller escalated before any trip details were gathered.

Before step 1: if caller_email_raw is already set from earlier in the call (the caller volunteered an email before this step), skip step 1 and go straight to step 2 (then step 4 onward), using caller_email_raw as the address to convert, check, and confirm.

1. Ask exactly one question: 'And an email for the confirmation?'
2. As you save it, convert what the caller says into true email-address form: spoken 'at' becomes '@', spoken 'dot' becomes '.', everything lowercase, and no spaces anywhere - never save the spoken words themselves (e.g. 'shane handel at gmail dot com' becomes '[REDACTED-owner-email]').
3. If the caller spells out any part of the email as they give it or right after (letter by letter, or a correction like 'that's a-n-d-e-l'), the spelled letters are the ground truth - apply them over whatever you thought you heard, even if it changes a word you initially understood clearly.
4. Check the structure of what you have: it needs exactly one '@' with something before it, and a domain after it containing at least one '.'. If a piece is missing or unclear, ask one targeted repair question naming exactly what's missing - e.g. 'I'm missing the at-sign - what's the full email?' or 'I didn't catch the domain after the at-sign - what's the full email?' - then re-apply steps 2-3 to the answer. This is your one repair pass - do not ask a second targeted repair question.
5. Once the address is structurally complete, spell the entire address back in one single grouped utterance - all letters and symbols back to back in one breath, saying 'at' for @ and 'dot' for . - then ask once, at the end, 'Did I get that right?' Never break the spell-back into multiple turns and never pause partway through to check in letter by letter or piece by piece; say the whole address once, then ask once. If the caller corrects it, apply the correction and do exactly one more full grouped spell-back to reconfirm - that is your one repair pass, whether the correction came before or after the first spell-back.
6. STOP CONDITION - check this every turn: if you have already done one repair pass (a targeted repair question, or a reconfirming spell-back after a correction) and the caller's response to that repair pass is anything other than a clear, unambiguous 'yes that's right' - including if they express any remaining doubt, hedge, or offer yet another variation - you MUST NOT attempt any further spell-back or repair question, no matter how tempting. Treat a reply as still-uncertain even when it opens with agreement-sounding words like 'yeah', 'pretty much', 'that's right', or 'basically' - if that same reply also restates, rephrases, adds to, or varies any part of the spelling or address, the whole reply counts as still-uncertain, not as confirmation, and the stop condition applies. Only a reply that is agreement with nothing else added counts as a clear confirmation. When the stop condition applies: in that very same turn, save whatever value you currently have, and say a sentence that clearly states the confirmation/receipt will be sent by text message instead (for example 'I'm not fully catching that - I'll text you the confirmation instead so you can double check it there.'). This sentence is mandatory in this situation - do not transition or move on without saying it.
7. If the caller declines to give an email, acknowledge briefly once, set email_declined to true, and do not ask again.
8. You must call save_caller_email before doing anything else next - do not transition, say goodbye, or say the call is ending until that tool call has been made with the confirmed (or declined, or best-effort-uncertain) value. Call it exactly once, with every value you have, in a single call - never call it more than once for the same decision.
9. Immediately after the tool call, transition - do not say goodbye, do not say the call is ending, and do not add any closing remarks yourself. A later step delivers the actual goodbye, not this one.
